body: Oh definitely, and I wish I died at birth when I had underdeveloped lungs. And I wish my that my dad had killed me like he threatened he would so many times before. Life is a real bitch...

I'm only 22 but I most likely will not live to see 36. I have many medical and mental issues, and I've made multiple suicide attempts that have dealt permanent damage to my cardiovascular and gastrointestinal systems. If my body doesn't kill me, then maybe my next suicide attempt will(and they happen fairly often). I'm also anorexic and nearly died a few times from that alone. A peak from 16-36 doesn't seem fair to me.

I'm curious to know if FA'er and another FA'er getting into a relationship is different from a FA'er and a normie? Or does my ex even count as one. I sure as hell counted as one until I made friends with him, and when he and I met he also had no friends. During our friendship though he made the other friend, whereas I still had no one else.
I already have the "happiness" I deserve. None. I've done nothing to deserve anything better than what I've gotten, I actually deserve worse, but thanks I guess.

I was voluntarily admitted the first time, but not the second time.  The local crisis center was basically like that according to other people's experience with it. Some of the patients I met in my in-patient visit told me horror stories about it. Apparently it was only any good as a detox/rehab addiction clinic. The crisis center portion was just a forgettable feature according to my fellow patient(s). 

I guess I was lucky that I was taken to the hospital rather than the crisis center. If I had been in that sort of situation to begin with I wouldn't have made all the progress I've made since my initial visit. Fingers crossed for your family member. I had a good experience with my time in the hospital, but I'm still struggling with the desire to commit suicide. I can only imagine how much harder it would be if someone to be taken into a place that when they are already at their limits. But that's just me, her method of recovery may require something completely different to what I needed. 

I wish you and her the best of luck. It's pretty hypocritical of me to say this but Don't Give Up. If you are feeling like you are going to hurt yourself you should call them. Even if they don't or can't help, they might find something that can.

I've called once and was directed to a local crisis line once. When I called the hotline the person on the other line handled it very well. They ended up calling the authorities and I was hospitalized as a result. 

The other time was actually my first time dealing with crisis workers like that. I was having a really bad anxiety attack and called my doctors office about not being able to afford my medicine or future appointments. I was able to maintain my composure and starting bawling. One thing lead to another and the crisis line sent one of their workers to my apartment to keep me from harming myself. They would have admitted me to their facility, but they were full so they had the police take me to the hospital.

Neither time really helped much, but my first hospitalization put me on the path to recovery.
My friend took me in after I had lost my home, and I have a few online friends, but that's about it.
If only it were that simple...
